# PropertyMax.ai Platform Overview

PropertyMax.ai is a comprehensive property management platform designed to streamline operations, track key performance indicators, and manage daily tasks for property managers and staff. Below is a detailed description of five key sections within the application.

---

## 1. Dashboard

The Dashboard serves as the central hub for property managers, providing a high-level overview of critical metrics and daily operations. It is designed to give users immediate visibility into the health of their properties. The top navigation bar displays the system health status (e.g., "Systems Healthy") and the last sync time, while providing quick access to various integrated tools such as Vacancy, AI Bot, AppWork, Inspections, Paychex, and Yardi.

A prominent **Collections Overview** widget displays financial metrics for the selected property for the current month. It shows the total amount billed, the amount collected, and the outstanding balance, allowing managers to quickly assess revenue performance. The Dashboard also includes sections dedicated to tracking delinquent accounts and pending tasks, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks. Users can view their personal tasks, guest card tasks, maintenance tasks, and rent-related tasks — each with a badge count for quick triage.

Communication is heavily integrated into the Dashboard. A comprehensive call log tracks incoming and outgoing calls, complete with audio playback, caller details, and an AI-generated sentiment summary (e.g., "Golden Score: 47% MARKETING"). It also includes a robust SMS interface showing recent text conversations with prospects and tenants, categorized by marketing and non-marketing messages. Finally, an **Inspections** widget provides quick access to upcoming and pending inspections, filterable by status and unit, showing the tenant name, scheduled date, and assigned inspector.

---

## 2. My Profile

The My Profile section is a personalized workspace for individual staff members, combining human resources information with a comprehensive daily schedule. It displays the user's full name, email address, phone number, hire date, and upcoming work anniversary date. An **Edit** button allows users to update their personal information directly.

A significant portion of the profile is dedicated to **time-off management**. It provides a detailed summary of accrued, used, and available sick time and vacation time in a structured table format. Users can initiate new time-off requests directly from this interface using the "Request" button.

The core of the My Profile section is an interactive, color-coded calendar view that consolidates the user's entire schedule for the current month. The calendar integrates multiple data streams simultaneously, as described below.

| Calendar Event Type | Color | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Inspections** | Dark/Navy | Scheduled unit inspections (e.g., move-in, final charges/pictures), showing the unit, tenant, and assigned inspector. |
| **Maintenance** | Red | Assigned work orders categorized by issue type (HVAC, Plumbing, Appliance, etc.) with the full problem description. |
| **Appointments** | Orange/Amber | Scheduled meetings, tours, or lease signings with prospects or tenants. |
| **Sick / Vacation / Co. Travel / Rent** | Various | Approved time-off events and rent-related calendar items. |

Users can toggle each event type on or off using the checkboxes in the color legend, and navigate between months using the previous/next arrows.

---

## 3. Reports

The Reports section provides analytical tools to help property managers make data-driven decisions. It is accessible via a dropdown in the main navigation bar. Currently, the primary report available is the **Marketing Report**.

This tool allows users to analyze lead generation sources for a specific property over a custom date range. Users select a property from a dropdown, set a "From Date" and "To Date," and click Submit to generate the report. The output is a horizontal bar chart displaying the count of referrals from each marketing channel. For a property like Pelican Bay, the tracked sources include Friends and Family, Apartments.com, Google, Driveby traffic, Facebook, affordablehousing.com, Housing Authorities, and Rent Path. This data is essential for evaluating the return on investment of different marketing campaigns and making informed decisions about where to allocate advertising spend.

---

## 4. Appointments

The Appointments module is a dedicated system for scheduling and managing all interactions with prospects, tenants, and vendors. It is surfaced directly on the Dashboard as a panel showing upcoming appointments with a badge count, and new appointments can be created from anywhere via the "+ New" button.

When creating a new appointment, users are presented with a detailed scheduling form with the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Building Name** | Auto-populated with the user's assigned property. |
| **Category** | Type of appointment: Tour, Signing, Maintenance, Vendor, Inquiry, Rent, or Other/Unknown. |
| **Unit** | The specific apartment unit associated with the appointment. |
| **Appointment Date** | The scheduled date and time. |
| **Caller / Recipient Phone** | Contact phone numbers for both parties. |
| **Tenant Guest Card** | Option to link the appointment to an existing tenant or add the contact as a new prospect. |
| **Appointment Summary** | A free-text area for detailed notes about the appointment's purpose and context. |

Appointments are displayed on the Dashboard with the date, time, and summary (e.g., "Mr. Pennywell confirmed move-in date for one bedroom on May 22, 2026"), and they also appear on the My Profile calendar for a unified schedule view.

---

## 5. Rental Comps

The Rental Comps (Comparables) section is a vital market intelligence tool that allows property managers to benchmark their rental rates against competing properties in the surrounding area. It is accessible from the main Dashboard and can be exported as a published sheet for external sharing or reporting.

The comparison table is organized into two distinct categories: **Affordable Comps** (properties participating in programs such as LIHTC, Section 8, or HUD, highlighted in green) and **Market Rate Comps** (properties with no income restrictions, highlighted in purple). The subject property (e.g., Pelican Bay) is prominently marked with a star at the top of the table.

For each competing property, the table provides the following data points across all unit types:

| Column | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Property** | Name of the competing apartment community. |
| **Location** | City and state. |
| **Proximity** | Distance from the subject property (color-coded by range). |
| **Low** | The lowest advertised rent for that unit type. |
| **High** | The highest advertised rent for that unit type. |
| **FMR** | The Fair Market Rent as established by HUD. |
| **Mkt Avg** | The calculated market average rent for that unit type. |

This data is displayed for 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, 3-bedroom, and 4-bedroom units side by side, enabling managers to instantly see how their pricing compares across the full unit mix. Competing properties tracked include Bon Carre' Court (Melrose), Newport Villa, Mt. Zion Homes, Howell Place, Sienna Lake Apartments, Willow Creek Apartments, The Preserve at Harveston, and Copper Mill Apartments.
